summary: Frontend-only testing of the two new offline features: 'Modelli Ricorrenti' (reusable materials/schema templates) and one-tap company logo on all documents. Mobile viewport 390x844. 18/19 automated UI checks passed; T17/T18 (PDF HTML content of img.logo in .doc-head) could not be programmatically captured because expo-print on web triggers the browser Print API via an inline iframe whose content is not reachable from Playwright. The underlying contract is verified by code review (document-html.ts line 173 inserts inside .doc-head for both DiCo and DiRi branches, and document/[id].tsx line 41 passes company.logo_uri converted to a data URI into generateHtml). Logo persistence (dico_company.logo_uri) and all testIDs required by the request are present. Browser session is per-invocation so all persistence tests ran inside the same session.

action_items: Non-blocking: on-device validation needed for the PDF logo (test on an actual Expo build / physical device by exporting a PDF and visually confirming the company logo appears in the top-left of DiCo and DiRi). Web preview cannot inspect the generated iframe used by expo-print.

Minor polish (optional): TemplateBar success message says 'Modello salvato ✓' only after save, but there is no analogous confirmation when a template is applied in save mode (apply shows 'Modello X applicato ✓' as expected). Already fine.

Minor note: react-native-web renders TextField as a bare (not
) when the TextField component is a thin wrapper. Playwright must use page.fill('[data-testid=template-name-input]', value) directly - no inner 'input' selector.
critical_code_review_comments: db.ts: new K_TEMPLATES key with listTemplates/saveTemplate/deleteTemplate is sound. ArchiveT.templates is optional in the type - exportAll and importAll both handle the field, so backup regression is OK.

LogoPicker uses expo-image-picker.launchImageLibraryAsync which creates a file input on web - verified via expect_file_chooser. On native the UI will prompt for photo-library permission; the 'blocked' fallback (logo-open-settings) is correctly wired.
document/[id].tsx (useEffect) correctly recomputes html when either doc or company changes, so an updated logo propagates to the preview without needing a reload.
generateHtml CSS places .logo as a float:left on .doc-head with max-height 56px / max-width 140px which should render well on both DiCo and DiRi headers.
TemplateBar canSave logic: materiali uses rows.length>0 and schema uses !isEmptySchema(schema); both correctly disable the save button.

No deprecated expo packages (expo-av/expo-barcode-scanner/expo-background-fetch) introduced in this iteration. Still using expo-image, expo-image-picker, expo-print, expo-file-system (legacy entry) which is acceptable.

success_rate.frontend: 18/19 automated UI checks (94.7%). 2 PDF HTML checks fall back to code review on web preview; one in-UI run of each new flow passes end-to-end.

seed_data_creation: Browser session only (not persistent across invocations): one 'TEST_MatModel' materiali template (then deleted via template-delete-0), one 'TEST_SchemaModel' schema template, one TEST_LogoCo company with uploaded /tmp/test_logo.png logo, two DICO-2026-0001 documents generated during flow. Nothing to clean up server-side.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Add to the standard testID list from iteration_2: company-logo-pick, company-logo-image, company-logo-change, company-logo-remove, logo-open-settings, template-materiali-load, template-materiali-save, template-materiali-msg, template-schema-load, template-schema-save, template-schema-msg, template-name-input (BARE <input> on web - use page.fill directly), template-save-confirm, template-item-{index}, template-delete-{index}, template-close, open-schema, schema-save, schema-cancel, schema-canvas, add-symbol-{key}, start-line, add-label, swatch-{color}. The web storage wrapper double-stringifies: localStorage values are JSON-encoded TWICE (storage.setItem wraps the already-JSON-string from writeJson), so decode with: let v=JSON.parse(raw); if (typeof v==='string') v=JSON.parse(v);  Expo-print on web is NOT inspectable from Playwright - its iframe is sandboxed. Use code review for PDF-content checks or run on-device. page.expect_file_chooser works for expo-image-picker on web.
rca_of_issue: N/A - no bugs reproduced in this iteration. Only one caveat is the inability to inspect the PDF output on web (expo-print architectural limitation, not a bug).
